newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul lowers number of Guam crash survivors to 30.
newsitem.headline: Seoul lowers number of Guam crash survivors to 30.

text.p: South Korean officials lowered to 30 from 55 the number of people who survived the crash of a Korean Air Lines (KAL) jumbo jet on the Pacific island of Guam on Wednesday, saying there had been miscommunications.

Deputy Foreign Minister Hong Jung-pyo said repeated checks showed that only 30 people were confirmed to have survived the crash. The latest figure still contradicted an account by the Guam Airport Authority, which put it at 35.
Korean Air Lines also revised its version on the number of survivors. KAL Vice President Lee Tae-won, who once raised the number to 61, reduced it to 33.
Lee said the confusion arose as they double-counted 28 survivors who were not seriously injured. He said of the 33, four had yet to be identified.
"All the survivors are at hospitals but we earlier believed that a further 28 people with minor injuries were rescued separately," Lee said.
KAL Flight 801, carrying 231 passengers and 23 crew crashed into a hilly area near Guam's airport early on Wednesday.
